quick: AML: 12 mg/m2/day IV x3 days with cytarabine
Can cause fetal harm; avoid; effective contraception
Reduce dose; do not give if bilirubin >5 mg/dL
LVEF/ECG, CBC, LFTs, renal function, infusion site
summary: Idarubicin is an anthracycline cytotoxic given intravenously, in combination with cytarabine, to induce remission in adult acute myeloid leukemia. It intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II. It carries boxed warnings for severe myelosuppression, dose-dependent cardiotoxicity (cardiomyopathy/heart failure), severe local tissue necrosis if extravasated, and the requirement for intravenous-only administration by clinicians experienced in cytotoxic therapy. Usual induction dose is 12 mg/m2/day IV for 3 days.
indications: In combination with other approved antileukemic drugs (e.g., cytarabine) for treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults, to induce remission

dosage.d: 12 mg/m2/day IV slow injection over 10-15 min for 3 days, with cytarabine
dosage.n: Cytarabine commonly 100 mg/m2/day continuous infusion x7 days

dosage.d: Reduce dose if bilirubin elevated; do NOT administer if bilirubin >5 mg/dL
Consider dose reduction when serum creatinine >2 mg/dL
Account for prior anthracycline lifetime dose; cardiotoxicity is cumulative
dosage.n: Monitor LVEF; discontinue if cardiac function declines

admin: For intravenous use ONLY - never give by intramuscular or subcutaneous route
Administer slowly (over 10-15 minutes) into the tubing of a freely running IV infusion of saline or dextrose
Avoid extravasation - it is a potent vesicant causing severe local necrosis; stop immediately and treat if it occurs
Handle and dispose of as a hazardous cytotoxic agent using appropriate precautions
Administer only under supervision of a physician experienced in leukemia chemotherapy with adequate supportive care available
moa: Idarubicin intercalates into DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II, blocking nucleic acid synthesis and DNA repair. It also generates free radicals. These actions, together with high lipophilicity that enhances cellular uptake, produce cell-cycle-disrupting cytotoxicity in rapidly dividing leukemic cells.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to idarubicin or other anthracyclines/anthracenediones
Severe hepatic impairment with bilirubin >5 mg/dL
relative: Pre-existing cardiac disease or reduced LVEF

preg: Idarubicin can cause fetal harm based on mechanism and animal data (embryotoxic and teratogenic). Avoid in pregnancy; advise women of childbearing potential to use effective contraception during and after therapy, and inform of potential fetal risk.
lact: It is not known whether idarubicin is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant, breastfeeding should be discontinued during treatment.
renal: Reduce the dose in renal impairment; consider dose reduction when serum creatinine exceeds 2 mg/dL. Assess renal function before each cycle.
hepatic: Idarubicin is extensively metabolized by the liver and excreted in bile; impairment increases exposure and toxicity. Reduce the dose in hepatic impairment and do not administer if bilirubin is greater than 5 mg/dL.

major: Other cardiotoxic agents (e.g., trastuzumab, high-dose cyclophosphamide) - additive cardiotoxicity
Live vaccines - risk of disseminated infection in immunosuppressed patients
moderate: Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy / radiotherapy - additive marrow suppression
Hepatotoxic drugs - increased hepatotoxicity and altered clearance
minor: Drugs affecting hepatic metabolism may alter idarubicinol levels
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol due to additive hepatotoxicity, nausea and bleeding risk during thrombocytopenia.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes pancytopenia, raises uric acid (tumor lysis), and may elevate liver enzymes/bilirubin; urine may turn red-orange transiently.

serious: Cardiotoxicity - cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure
emergency: Tumor lysis syndrome with hyperkalemia/renal failure

monitoring: Baseline and periodic LVEF (echocardiogram/MUGA) and ECG
Frequent complete blood counts during therapy
Liver function (bilirubin, transaminases) and renal function before each cycle
Uric acid and electrolytes for tumor lysis syndrome
Injection site for extravasation; oral cavity for mucositis
counsel: This chemotherapy is given only into a vein by trained staff
Report any burning or pain at the injection site immediately
Your urine may turn reddish for 1-2 days, which is harmless
Watch for fever, sore throat, bleeding or bruising and report promptly - your blood counts will drop
Tell your team about breathlessness, swelling or palpitations (signs of heart strain)
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed during treatment
pk: Immediate systemic exposure after IV dose
Plasma peak at end of injection; rapid tissue distribution
Idarubicin ~22 h; active idarubicinol ~45 h or longer
Active metabolite gives prolonged cytotoxic exposure
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C; protect from light
pearls: Boxed warnings: severe myelosuppression, cardiotoxicity, IV-only administration, and severe tissue necrosis with extravasation
Cardiotoxicity is cumulative - track lifetime anthracycline dose and monitor LVEF
Highly lipophilic; the active metabolite idarubicinol has a long half-life and contributes to activity
Do not give if bilirubin >5 mg/dL; reduce dose for hepatic/renal impairment
Treat extravasation as an emergency (stop infusion, aspirate, cold compress, consider dexrazoxane)
missed: Not applicable - idarubicin is administered on a defined inpatient/clinic chemotherapy schedule by healthcare professionals; missed or delayed doses are managed by the oncology team, not self-corrected.
overdose: Overdose intensifies myelosuppression, mucositis and acute/delayed cardiotoxicity. There is no specific antidote. Provide intensive supportive care including transfusions, antibiotics for neutropenic infection, management of mucositis, and treatment of heart failure. Idarubicin is not appreciably removed by dialysis.
